accepted.s: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 was sent to India by the British Prime Minister who was:
accepted.x: The Cabinet Mission was sent by Clement Attlee's Labour Government after the Second World War.
accepted.tq: Use the sponsoring authority and avoid confusing the wartime and post-war British Prime Ministers.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Cabinet Mission arrived in India on:
accepted.x: The Mission arrived in India on 24 March 1946 and announced its plan on 16 May 1946.
accepted.tq: Separate the date of arrival from the date on which the plan was announced.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Cabinet Mission Plan was announced on:
accepted.x: The Cabinet Mission announced its constitutional proposals on 16 May 1946.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely related dates by linking each date to its specific event.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 was also known as the:
accepted.x: Because it consisted of three British Cabinet Ministers, the Cabinet Mission was known as the Ministerial Trio Mission.
accepted.tq: Test the exact official or popular designation rather than the broad purpose of the body.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Member)
a. Lord Pethick-Lawrence
b. Sir Stafford Cripps
c. A.V. Alexander

List-II (Office held in Britain)
i. First Lord of the Admiralty

option_a: a-ii, b-iii, c-i
option_b: a-i, b-ii, c-iii
option_c: a-iii, b-i, c-ii

accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the immediate purpose of the Cabinet Mission in India?
o: To supervise the first general election under the Constitution
To establish a permanent military government under the Viceroy
To organise a plebiscite on the partition of Punjab and Bengal
To set up machinery for framing India's Constitution and arrange an Interim Government
accepted.x: The Mission aimed to establish machinery for framing India's Constitution and to arrange an Interim Government.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise two-part purpose instead of selecting a related constitutional development.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
The Cabinet Mission rejected the demand for a separate Pakistan primarily because:
1. The north-western and north-eastern zones contained substantial non-Muslim populations.
2. Partitioning Punjab and Bengal would disrupt their regional and economic ties.
3. It considered an undivided India preferable to the proposed division.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the reasons for rejecting a full Pakistan. The non-Muslim populations were noted as 38% in the north-west and 48% in the north-east.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of reasons together while checking whether each statement supports the same constitutional conclusion.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the Cabinet Mission Plan, the Union of India was to deal only with which subjects?
accepted.x: The proposed Union had a deliberately weak Centre responsible only for Defence, Foreign Affairs and Communications.
accepted.tq: Use the limited-subject feature to distinguish the proposed Union from a strong central federation.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the three-tier structure proposed by the Cabinet Mission, consider the following statements:
1. The first tier was the Union of India.
2. The second tier consisted of groups of provinces.
3. The provinces retained all residuary subjects.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The plan proposed a Union, provincial groups and individual provinces. The provinces were to hold all residuary subjects.
accepted.tq: Check the structure from the highest tier to the lowest and include the residuary-power provision.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following provinces was included in Group A under the Cabinet Mission Plan?
accepted.x: Group A comprised Madras, Bombay, the United Provinces, Bihar, the Central Provinces and Orissa.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between provinces belonging to the three proposed groups.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets represents Group B under the Cabinet Mission Plan?
o: Punjab, North-West Frontier Province and Sindh
accepted.x: Group B consisted of Punjab, the North-West Frontier Province and Sindh, forming the Muslim-majority north-western group.
accepted.tq: Match the regional group with its complete provincial composition rather than with a single province.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Group A — Hindu-majority provinces
2. Group B — Muslim-majority north-western provinces
3. Group C — Muslim-majority north-eastern provinces

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Group A was Hindu-majority, while Groups B and C represented the Muslim-majority north-western and north-eastern zones respectively.
accepted.tq: Compare each group by both its geographical location and communal character.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following provinces belonged to Group C under the Cabinet Mission Plan?
accepted.x: Group C consisted of Bengal and Assam.
accepted.tq: Use the group-wise provincial lists to distinguish Group C from the north-western Group B.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Constituent Assembly established under the Cabinet Mission Plan was intended to consist of:
accepted.x: The proposed Constituent Assembly had 389 members: 296 from British India and 93 from the princely states.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the total membership from its two component figures.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the composition of the Constituent Assembly under the Cabinet Mission Plan, consider the following statements:
1. British India was allotted 296 seats.
2. Princely states were allotted 93 seats.
3. The seats were distributed roughly in the ratio of one representative per ten lakh of population.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Assembly had 296 representatives from British India and 93 from princely states, with representation based approximately on one seat per ten lakh population.
accepted.tq: Combine numerical allocation with the population-based rule and verify all three details.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The representatives of the princely states in the Constituent Assembly were to be:
o: Nominated by the rulers of the princely states
Directly elected by the people of the states
Elected by the provincial legislative assemblies
accepted.x: The representatives of the princely states were to be nominated by their respective rulers.
accepted.tq: Ask who exercised the appointing authority and distinguish nomination from indirect election.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The seats allotted to the provinces in the Constituent Assembly were divided among which communities?
accepted.x: Provincial seats were divided among General, Muslim and Sikh communities.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact constitutional categories rather than substituting broader social classifications.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
The provincial representatives to the Constituent Assembly were elected by:
1. The provincial assemblies.
2. Separate members of the respective General, Muslim and Sikh communities.
3. Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Provincial assembly members elected representatives through community-wise voting using proportional representation by the single transferable vote.
accepted.tq: Break the election method into electorate, community division and voting system.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following provisions was also associated with the Cabinet Mission Plan?
1. All members of the Interim Cabinet were to be Indians.
2. The Viceroy's interference in the Interim Cabinet was to be minimised.
3. India was recognised as having the right to leave the Commonwealth.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The plan envisaged an Indian Interim Cabinet with minimum Viceroy interference and recognised India's right to leave the Commonwealth.
accepted.tq: Check whether each constitutional safeguard belongs to the same plan.
accepted.sec: Cabinet Mission - members, purpose, three-tier structure, groupings (A, B, C), Constituent Assembly method  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the Interim Government, Jawaharlal Nehru served as:
o: Vice-President of the Viceroy's Executive Council and in charge of External Affairs and Commonwealth Relations
President of the Viceroy's Executive Council
Finance Member and Leader of the Muslim League
Defence Member and President of the Executive Council
accepted.x: Nehru was Vice-President of the Viceroy's Executive Council and held External Affairs and Commonwealth Relations. The Viceroy remained the President of the Council.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the formal constitutional head from the political head of the Interim Government.
accepted.sec: Interim Government - date, plan that envisaged it, head, portfolios, League's entry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who continued to be the President of the Viceroy's Executive Council during the Interim Government?
accepted.x: Lord Wavell remained President of the Viceroy's Executive Council, while Nehru served as its Vice-President.
accepted.tq: Separate the nominal constitutional office from the effective political leadership.
accepted.sec: Interim Government - date, plan that envisaged it, head, portfolios, League's entry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly matches the Muslim League nominees with their portfolios in the Interim Government?
o: Liaquat Ali Khan—Finance; Jogendra Nath Mandal—Law
Liaquat Ali Khan—Defence; Jogendra Nath Mandal—Labour
Liaquat Ali Khan—Home; Jogendra Nath Mandal—External Affairs
Liaquat Ali Khan—Food and Agriculture; Jogendra Nath Mandal—Finance
accepted.x: Liaquat Ali Khan held the Finance portfolio and Jogendra Nath Mandal held the Law portfolio.
accepted.tq: Use the League nominees and their portfolios as a paired recall unit.
accepted.sec: Interim Government - date, plan that envisaged it, head, portfolios, League's entry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Muslim League joined the Interim Government in:
accepted.x: The Muslim League entered the Interim Government in October 1946.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of the original formation from the month of League participation.
accepted.sec: Interim Government - date, plan that envisaged it, head, portfolios, League's entry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following persons made way for Muslim League nominees when the League entered the Interim Government?
1. Sarat Chandra Bose
2. Shafaat Ahmed Khan
3. Syed Ali Zaheer

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Sarat Chandra Bose, Shafaat Ahmed Khan and Syed Ali Zaheer made way for the League nominees.
accepted.tq: Test a named three-person list through complete-set recognition.
accepted.sec: Interim Government - date, plan that envisaged it, head, portfolios, League's entry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Liaquat Ali Khan's 'poor man's budget' was politically significant because it:
o: Transferred the Defence portfolio to the Muslim League
Provided funds exclusively for princely states
Reduced taxation on Indian business to strengthen Congress support
Taxed Indian business heavily and was used to embarrass Congress members
accepted.x: As Finance Member, Liaquat Ali Khan introduced the 'poor man's budget' in 1947, which heavily taxed Indian business and embarrassed Congress members.
accepted.tq: Apply the economic measure to its political purpose instead of treating it as an ordinary budget fact.
accepted.sec: Interim Government - date, plan that envisaged it, head, portfolios, League's entry  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: The idea of a Constituent Assembly was first accepted through the August Offer of 1940.
The Constituent Assembly was indirectly elected by provincial assemblies on the basis of population.
The Constituent Assembly was directly elected by all adult citizens of British India in 1946.
The Cabinet Mission Plan envisaged the Interim Government.
accepted.x: The Constituent Assembly was not directly elected by universal adult franchise; its provincial members were indirectly elected by provincial assemblies. The August Offer had accepted the idea of a constitution-making body.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses indirect election into direct universal election.
accepted.sec: Interim Government - date, plan that envisaged it, head, portfolios, League's entry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly distinguishes the origins of the Constituent Assembly idea?
1. M.N. Roy demanded the idea in 1934.
2. The Congress adopted the demand in 1935.
3. The August Offer of 1940 accepted the idea of a constitution-making body.
4. The Cabinet Mission Plan provided the scheme under which the Assembly was formed.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: M.N. Roy raised the demand in 1934, Congress adopted it in 1935, the August Offer accepted the idea in 1940, and the Cabinet Mission Plan provided the formation scheme.
accepted.tq: Trace the development from the original demand to the constitutional mechanism that implemented it.
accepted.sec: Interim Government - date, plan that envisaged it, head, portfolios, League's entry  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Demand for a Constituent Assembly by M.N. Roy
B. Adoption of the demand by the Congress
C. Acceptance of the constitution-making body in the August Offer
D. Announcement of the Cabinet Mission Plan
accepted.x: M.N. Roy's demand dates to 1934, the Congress adopted it in 1935, the August Offer accepted it in 1940, and the Cabinet Mission Plan was announced in 1946.
accepted.tq: Fix the first two milestones and then place the later constitutional proposals.
accepted.sec: Interim Government - date, plan that envisaged it, head, portfolios, League's entry  [APPSC]
